findings.finding: The Q3 report carries a line the market has not seen: management said in Q2 it would return 'during the third quarter' with a more detailed description of cost synergies from Amesto, Exsitec's largest acquisition ever (adds ~25% to revenue). This sits on top of an already-booked ~MSEK 10/yr Norway restructuring saving.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior synergy quantification to compare against. The Amesto deal announcement itself (2026-05-20, 13:00 CEST, inside information) coincided with a +13.1% session.
findings.original_quote: The integration work has commenced according to plan, and we intend to return during the third quarter with a more detailed description of cost synergies from the acquisition.
findings.why_not_priced: No synergy number has been published. If it were priced, the stock would not sit at ~11x trailing adj. EBITA with three broker targets of SEK 164-170 against a SEK 109 spot. The cross-check: SB1's own initiation case leans on Amesto EBITA growth, and the stock moved only +3.8% on that note and then gave it back.
findings.independence: SB1 Markets initiation expects EBITA growth partly from Amesto: https://www.placera.se/telegram/exsitec-sb1-markets-inleder-bevakning-av-exsitec-med-kop--ser-60-procents-uppsida-20261008

findings.finding: Organic momentum going into Q3 is company-documented: Q2 organic growth was 8% (7% in local currency) against 1% in Q1, order intake rose ~8% against a record Q2 2025, and the CEO called it 'a good starting position for the coming quarters', with Sweden improving.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On verified report days, organic and margin surprises moved the stock +11.4% (Q3 2025, adj. EBITA 25 vs 6), +4.6% (Q1 2026) and +2.5% (Q2 2026), but -12.7% on the Q4 2025 report despite adj. EBITA +43%.
findings.original_quote: Compared to a record-strong second quarter last year, order intake increased by approximately 8%, providing us with a good starting position for the coming quarters.
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced: this is public since July, and the stock has gone sideways since (104 on 10 July, 109 now). If the market fully expected an organic acceleration to carry through, the price would have re-rated toward the brokers' targets. It is sized small because it is a public statement that forecasts the quarter, not a number for it.
findings.independence: Placera/Finwire Q2 coverage: 'Bolaget uppger att de ser en gradvis förbättrad efterfrågan främst i Sverige' https://www.placera.se/telegram/exsitec-exsitec-rapporterar-organisk-tillvaxt-pa-7-procent-i-q2-20260710

findings.finding: Denmark is a known drag: the Other Nordics adj. EBITA margin collapsed to 5.2% (15.7%) in Q2 on weak order intake, weak demand from existing customers and poor consulting efficiency. Capacity was cut in Q2, but Q3 is seasonally the weakest quarter for absorbing that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Segment-level misses have not been isolated in prior reactions. The -12.7% on 2026-02-03 came on a report with group margin up, which suggests the name can sell on growth or segment quality.
findings.original_quote: The lower profitability is attributable to Denmark and is explained by weak order intake, low demand from existing customers, and lower-than-desired efficiency in the consulting operations.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, because it is public. Net of the rest of the company: Other Nordics is the smallest segment, so Sweden (24.4% margin) and Norway, now with Amesto, decide the group. It would take a further leg down in Denmark to matter, hence the small size.

findings.finding: Coverage widened just before the print: SB1 Markets initiated at Buy with a SEK 170 target on 2026-10-08, joining Pareto (SEK 165, 2026-06-24) and Nordea (SEK 164, 2026-06-10). A third broker now models the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose +3.8% on the initiation day (106.5 to 110.5) and then drifted back to 109.
findings.original_quote: SB1 Markets inleder bevakning av Exsitec med köp – ser 60 procents uppsida
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced (wire copy, day-one reaction already given back). Its only print-day relevance is a wider audience for an in-line or better report, so it is sized near zero.

baseline_tension: Mild positive findings sit against a -6.4% 20-day run-up. The priced lean (+0.32) comes from the run-up alone because there is no short anchor, so the findings agree weakly with the lean and add little beyond it.

lessons_applied: 'Understatement / you were too small about the move' and 'size on what is new': abs_move_pct raised from 6.5 to 7.0. The period is not pre-released, it is the first full Amesto quarter and turnover is thin; the name's own ~5.5% verified median is used as context, not a cap
'Unsourced bar caps every finding, p_up toward 50': p_up lowered from 55 to 54, findings kept small

'reported_quarter findings went 4 of 14 / a number the market was told is worth ~0': the order-intake finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3 and the Denmark finding from -0.4 to -0.3, because both rest on Q2 statements that are already public
'The move is in the guide': the synergy description is the closest thing this no-guidance company has to a guidance line, so it stays the largest finding at +0.8, unchanged
